scores.evidence: It works offline and peer-to-peer, the server can be simple, and the libraries are mature.
scores.rationale: Mostly correct (Yjs, state vectors, relative positions, UndoManager), but "server can be simple" understates needs, and the plan omits that CRDT doesn't guarantee intent for rich-text conflicts, and "CRDT garbage collection" is glossed.

scores.evidence: Scope for v1: rich text, live cursors, sharing, offline editing, version history. Leave tables, embeds and comments for later.
scores.rationale: Covers core needs with explicit deferrals, though Phase 10 comments contradicts the v1 deferral and large-doc handling is thin.

scores.evidence: Alternatively, run several servers and share updates between them through Redis pub/sub.
scores.rationale: Mostly consistent, but scaling is deferred to phase 11 with two alternative routing options unresolved, comments deferred then scheduled, and Phase 1 builds a non-CRDT editor with its own undo later replaced.

scores.evidence: the fuzz tests pass across thousands of random runs, and the two side-by-side editors always end up the same.
scores.rationale: Risky convergence is tested early and gates are checkable, with load, offline and security tests, but some thresholds (500 ms, 2x peak) are invented and post-launch validation is thin.

scores.evidence: Targets: maximum users per document, maximum document size, and latency (for example, under 100 ms on the same continent).
scores.rationale: Team size and stack are stated as choices and targets are deferred, but there is little on which assumptions would change the design, and the 4-month timeline is asserted.

scores.evidence: Permissions bypassed over the socket | Server-side enforcement of every write (Phase 5)
scores.rationale: Risk table and tests cover divergence, log growth, permission bypass, oversized messages, and paste XSS, but revocation on open connections, poison updates, crash recovery and duplicates are not detailed.

scores.evidence: metrics for sync delay, connected clients, update throughput, compaction time and errors. Also distributed tracing and alerts.
scores.rationale: Observability, backups, feature-flag staged rollout exist but rollback, migrations, on-call ownership and protocol upgrades are not covered, and observability is left to the end.

scores.evidence: Suggested team (about 4–6 people, about 4 months to v1)
scores.rationale: Only team cost is given; infrastructure cost drivers (storage, connections, memory, S3) and controls are essentially absent beyond limits and idle unloading.

scores.evidence: Define the document schema: paragraphs, headings, lists, bold/italic, links.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 ADR and the log-based restore are good, but the schema is defined before the CRDT choice is bound, the persisted update format and schema versioning are not treated as one-way, and there are no exit paths.

scores.evidence: Do this once the features work. If you design for it earlier, just make sure documents are kept separate from each other
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate using off-the-shelf Yjs/Hocuspocus with optional items deferred, with minor extras such as a read-only fan-out tier, distributed tracing and a full dashboard.

scores.evidence: Each phase ends with a check that must pass before the next phase starts.
scores.rationale: Phases are concrete with week ranges, gates and dependency graph, though it doesn't say what to do if the gates fail and some decisions are left open.

checklist.evidence: Recommended: CRDT (for example Yjs, or Automerge). ... OT (as in Google Docs) needs a central server to decide the order of edits
Define the document schema: paragraphs, headings, lists, bold/italic, links.
Write convergence fuzz tests: random concurrent edits, delays and reordering, then check that all copies end up identical.
Make sure that when the server confirms an update, that update has been saved to disk.
Handle reconnection on the client with exponential backoff.
Cache documents and pending updates locally in IndexedDB (y-indexeddb).
Check permissions when the WebSocket connects using a short-lived token. Reject writes from viewers on the server
Replace normal undo with per-user undo (Y.UndoManager) ... Restore a version by writing a new update
This data is temporary and is not saved.
Phase 1: Single-user editor ... Phase 2: Local collaboration with no network (This is the most important phase)
Rate limits, a maximum document size, and protection against oversized messages.

traps.evidence: CRDT library, fuzz tests in Phase 2
Get editing right for one person before adding collaboration.
when the server confirms an update, that update has been saved to disk.
It works offline and peer-to-peer, the server can be simple

note: Sound CRDT-first plan with early fuzz testing and concrete phases, but it is weak on cost, protocol/schema versioning, rich-text merge semantics and operations, and it starts with a single-user editor.
